Changelog

What changed, and when

This is curated from the repository's own history. Releases are listed newest first. The current release is 1.6.4, and the entry above it is work on main that has not been cut into a release yet.

  1. 3.0.0 · 20 October 2026

    Standalone sign-in, a demo that reaches its instance, and a version that says what it is

    • The sign-in and registration pages now stand alone. The shell that was meant to hide was not hiding: a component that sets its own display beats the browser's rule for the hidden attribute, so the empty shell kept the viewport and pushed the page below it.
    • The demo and the community directory reach the instance again. The public site and the API are different origins in a real deployment, and the pages were asking for a relative path that the site cannot answer; they now resolve the address the same way the application does.
    • The deployment build was shipping an old tree: it fetched the newest source and then checked out the branch it already had. It now deploys what it fetched.
    • Instance discovery, per-instance sessions, an in-house search index, backups with a restore path, housekeeping, and one honest report per subsystem all land in this release.
    • The version is reported by the server, the API and the application, and all of them say the same thing.

  2. 2.5.0 · 19 October 2026

    One backend, a chosen instance, and a machine that is not fighting itself

    • The backend was consolidated on backend/: the features and tables that lived only in the legacy server/ package were merged in, and a production instance now runs one backend instead of the split that had drifted.
    • The application was put on the canonical asset library: one generated set of design tokens that the app, the themes and the website all read.
    • A configuration centre was added where every setting shown actually does something, and mail gained a provider registry with an admin console.
    • Registration approval was added, with the migration parity check that had been missing.
    • Realtime naming was made consistent across the gateway and the client, kept in agreement by a check rather than by discipline.
    • This public site was rebuilt as its own composition, with a working demo and a public community directory, instead of a smaller copy of the app's layout.
    • Registration now takes an instance: browse the instances an instance knows about, or give the address of one you run. The address is checked against that instance before it is accepted, and a session belongs to the instance that issued it, so switching never carries a token across.
    • Search became an in-house index that works on every database this runs on, and the permission check lives inside it: a message from a community you are not in cannot answer a query.
    • Backups can be taken from the administration page and put back with a command that verifies the dump first and asks for the database name before it replaces anything.
    • The administration pages grew a rail, so every settings door and every moderation queue is one click away, and a diagnostics page that reports each subsystem as it really is rather than as its configuration implies.
    • The voice path is the in-house one, and an administrator's saved choice is what takes effect: the provider used to be read from the environment, which meant a setting that saved and changed nothing.
    • Housekeeping came with the jobs: expired sessions, old notifications and finished work are cleaned up on a rhythm that survives a restart.
    • The automated check suite was removed. It booted whole instances and started browsers, and on a small host it was more load than the product was worth; verification is now a real journey against a running instance.
    • Plain-language passes on error messages, settings and navigation.

  3. 1.6.4 · 3 October 2026

    Attachments, replies, and a release step that runs anywhere

    • Attachments in direct messages as well as communities, a tray you can see and undo, and a full-screen lightbox.
    • Replies, with a badge that follows the message it answers.
    • Rich link previews with a per-message opt-out, and an endpoint that declares its arguments instead of guessing.
    • Embeds, analytics and webhooks, and bot applications, behind a single permission gate.
    • The client is told its own server: a self-hosted instance stops advertising someone else's backend, and the server can find the client next to itself.
    • Release verification moved to bash so it runs on every platform, and the browser checks were brought into the repository.

  4. 1.6.3 · 27 September 2026

    One seeded role, and the owner inherits everything

    • @everyone is the only seeded role and the community baseline. The owner inherits every permission from ownership rather than from a role, so no Admin or Moderator roles are created for them.
    • Fixed a bug that made the baseline role unconfigurable, and removed self-assignable roles end to end.
    • Context menus added for notifications, friends, invites and search results.
    • The render-crash watchdog no longer mistakes a valid sign-in screen for a hang, and the desktop app gained CORS diagnostics for its own scheme.

  5. 1.6.2 · 26 September 2026

    Contextual navigation and a full-width workspace

    • Navigation rebuilt around contextual shells: a home sidebar and a menu page, with the mobile drawer removed.
    • The workspace layout rebuilt around a full-width chat view, with loading and empty states and a hover bar.
    • A theme system overhaul, including a client that heals itself instead of rendering a blank window when a render crashes.
    • One uniform template across every static public page.

  6. 1.6.1 · 25 September 2026

    Desktop publishing and the portable build

    • Desktop builds published to the project repository, with the portable Windows build named TrycordPTB.

  7. 1.6.0 and 1.5.0 · 23 September 2026

    Themes, and the design system reconciled

    • A seven-theme ecosystem: token-override themes and a custom palette derivation.
    • The appearance interface with persistence, and the theme restored at boot.
    • The written design system was reconciled with the code so the two could not quietly disagree.

  8. 1.0.1 · 20 September 2026

    No more blank page on an updated client

    • The server never serves a stale client bundle; it shows a reload notice instead of a blank page.

  9. 0.5.0 · 19 September 2026

    Self-hosting, and a configurable database

    • The client serve path, runtime configuration, and instance state.
    • MySQL and SQLite adapters behind one interface, with a validated boot.
    • CORS origins and the /api/instance endpoint other client work depends on.

For the commit-level record, the repository history is the source this page is drawn from. Releases are published on GitHub.
